recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Avoid adding duplicate wording to the workflow pages unless a future work-group decision reopens core workflow cancellation/revision guidance; the current source is semantically aligned with FHIR-14779.
issue_request: FHIR-14779 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the STU3 FHIR-core workflow page. It said non-Task request/fulfillment patterns appeared unable to cancel an order, making Task seem necessary in most contexts; the accepted resolution directed that order cancellation and order revision be discussed in each scenario while noting cancellation is not relevant to every order or workflow.
initial_application: Jira's SVN #14780 comment corresponds to git-svn commit 2787aa8c73ec559cfd0ca2c2f94104c954592783, 'Workflow clarifications: 14778, 14779, 15703'. That commit added cancellation guidance to source/workflow-ad-hoc.html and source/workflow-management.html, including custom operations, Request status cancellation, polling/subscription limitations, purpose-specific messages, Task cancellation by the placer, and fulfiller/broker control over whether a Task can be cancelled.
additional_context: The workflow pages are still current build-facing informative documentation, linked from source/documentation.html and source/workflow-module.html. Later source changes retained the cancellation guidance; current workflow-management text also covers request status changes and other updates, and source/workflow-communications.html includes a cancellation-and-revised-referral example. Direct FHIR-14779 Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting community record, and broader order-workflow hits were later Clinical Order Workflow material rather than a FHIR-core reversal.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already tells implementers that Task is useful for workflow management, negotiation, progress, cancellation, and updates, while some non-Task patterns can handle cancellation or revision through custom operations, Request updates, purpose-specific messages, or replacement requests, with limitations called out.

related_jiras.note: The same historical SVN/git commit also applied a workflow page relocation request; it helped identify the original application context but was not decided here.
The same historical SVN/git commit also bundled a small wording fix unrelated to the cancellation/revision audit.
